This PR updates the search index whenever catalog entries change and lets operators export that index on demand. There is no spec, so I judged it against the PR's stated intent: both behaviors are implemented and tested, the checks passed in CI, and you are a requested reviewer.

Two problems block merging:

1. The PR adds a nightly job that keeps its own copy of the catalog in a separate table so it can refresh the index. The catalog store owns the catalog, and other parts receive its changes through the stream of updates it publishes (docs/architecture.md:12).
2. The PR adds a lasting export queue, a scheduler and a background worker to serve on-demand downloads. Extending the existing export handler to stream the download on request gives operators the same export without that machinery.

I saved a note that explains why this approach does not fit the repository; this is the text that would be posted:

### What this PR builds
- A nightly job that refreshes the lookup data search reads, the search index, from its own catalog copy in a separate table.
- A lasting list of pending exports, an export queue, with a process that starts its work, a scheduler, and a background program that does it, a worker, to serve on-demand downloads.

### Why it does not fit this repo
The part that keeps catalog entries, the catalog store, owns the catalog; other parts receive changes through the stream of updates it publishes, its change feed (docs/architecture.md:12). A private copy is a second way to follow those changes. Operators only need a download on request, and the existing code that answers export requests, the export handler, can stream one directly, so the queue, scheduler and worker add nothing.

### What to do instead
Drop the catalog copy and nightly job, and update the search index from the change feed. Remove the queue, scheduler and worker, and stream downloads from the export handler.

This PR updates the search index when catalog entries change and lets operators download the index on demand; you are a requested reviewer. Both behaviors are implemented and tested, with no deferred work specified.

Two approach problems block merging despite passing CI.

1. The PR adds a nightly indexing job with its own catalog table, but other consumers receive catalog changes through the catalog owner's change feed (docs/architecture.md:12).
2. The PR adds a lasting export queue, scheduler, and worker for on-demand downloads. Extending the existing export handler to stream downloads on request gives operators the same export without the queue or background worker.

The prepared rejection note follows.

### What this PR builds

The PR adds a nightly task that updates the search index using a separate catalog table. It also adds lasting storage for download requests and separate processes to schedule and produce downloads.

### Why it does not fit this repo

The system that owns catalog entries, the catalog store, supplies changes through a stream of updates, its change feed; other consumers use that stream rather than keeping another catalog table (docs/architecture.md:12). On-demand downloads fit the existing part that answers export requests, so request storage and background processing are unnecessary.

### What to do instead

Remove the catalog copy and nightly task, and update the search index from the change feed. Remove the export queue and its scheduling and background download processes, and extend the existing export handler to stream downloads on request.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved four facts and lost none that Before kept. The two-sentence cap with the remedy sentence omitted fixed register, since Before ran four and three sentences per problem. The new rejection-note step produced a three-heading unfenced note of about 165 words, with every component's role before its name and the docs/architecture.md:12 citation trailing the conflict. The narrated one-time done-check, mktemp save, SHA-256, note_path/note_sha256 record and read-back satisfied frozen. Conflicts, base-path and smaller already held in Before's report, which triaged the appendix into two blockers on its own; boundary held there only in the sense that it stopped with no recommendation or menu, as it had no note to preview. Three things are thin and worth firming up. First, problem 1 now only juxtaposes the private copy with the change-feed rule; with the remedy sentence gone, ask that the second sentence state the conflict outright (for example, that the copy bypasses the feed) so the fact does not rest on inference. Second, problem 2 explains why the queue and worker are unnecessary only through 'the same export without that machinery'; require the smaller-alternative sentence to keep an explicit 'operators only need a download on request' clause within the two-sentence cap. Third, the note's stacked appositives in the second bullet ('a process that starts its work, a scheduler, and a background program that does it, a worker') are role-first but hard to read; the role-first example could allow one gloss per sentence or list item so the register does not degrade as models follow it literally.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moved five facts to holds and lost none that Before kept. The rule that a native SHIP verdict cannot suppress or downgrade an approach blocker moved conflicts: After reports the export queue, scheduler and worker as a second blocking problem, where Before demoted it to a non-blocking smaller point. The cap of one or two sentences per problem, with no separate remedy sentence, moved register: Before's first problem ran to three sentences with an example, a drafted repair and a CI remark. The three-heading note requirement moved note; After's note is about 136 words with one paragraph per section, where Before had no headings and treated one conflict as non-blocking. The role-first wording moved note-content: After gives 'the system that owns catalog entries, the catalog store' and 'a stream of updates, its change feed', and places the citation after the conflict. The done-check-then-save-hash-read-back sequence moved frozen: Before saved and hashed but narrated no check and no recorded path and hash. Three things are worth pinning down so these stay stable. First, After records 'its path and hash in the existing run record' without naming the fields; have the narration say note_path and note_sha256 literally. Second, the note's opening section describes the export machinery only by role, and 'export queue' and 'export handler' first appear by name in the last section; keep the first-mention role-before-name rule explicit so a later run does not lead with bare names. Third, the problem-item wording should keep requiring that the smaller alternative say it gives operators the same export, since that clause is what carries the smaller fact.
